title: Monitoring Insurers who Raise Base Integrated Shield Plan Premiums that Negate New Rider Savings
what_it_is: Monitoring Insurers who Raise Base Integrated Shield Plan Premiums that Negate New Rider Savings

sections.label: Private hospital IP and rider premiums
sections.summary: Private hospital IP premiums rose an average 8.6% yearly and rider premiums 17.2% yearly from December 2021 to December 2024, but new riders can save policyholders 35% to 40%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Across a three-year period from December 2021 to December 2024, private hospital IP premiums have been rising every year at an average of 8.6% while private hospital rider premiums have been rising every year at an average of 17.2%.
In line with these trends, some private hospital IP and rider plans were recently repriced.
However, with the launch of the new riders, policyholders can save on average 35% to 40% premiums by switching to the new riders.

sections.label: MOH regulation of IPs
sections.summary: MOH regulates key IP parameters like co-payment and deductible but generally does not intervene in insurers' commercial decisions such as premium setting.

sentences.text: While the Ministry of Health (MOH) regulates the key parameters of IPs, such as the co-payment and deductible, to ensure that the schemes are sustainable, MOH's general practice is not to intervene in insurers' commercial decisions, such as the setting of premiums.

sections.label: MAS action against insurers
sections.summary: MAS will take action against insurers who do not pay claims according to policy terms or who have unfair claims handling practices.

sentences.text: MAS will also take action against insurers if they do not pay claims in accordance with policy terms and conditions or have unfair claims handling practices.

sections.label: Causes and measures for healthcare costs
sections.summary: Causes include ageing population and technological advancements, with measures including fee benchmarks, clinical guidance, enforcement against errant providers, rider reforms and not-for-profit private hospitals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: As I mentioned earlier, there are the causes in relation to ageing population, technological advancements and we have measures and levers where we look at getting the most cost-effective products in the market.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We are also looking at how we can address the issue of over-servicing, over-consumption by putting in the levers that we have in place, which we have discussed previously in questions the Member has raised before, which includes fee benchmarks, clinical guidance to ensure that appropriate care is given and we enforce against errant providers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We have rider reforms, which the Member has seen; and also, in the works, the development of not-for-profit private hospitals.

sections.label: Cheaper riders and subsidised public healthcare
sections.summary: Cheaper riders are an option, and access to subsidised services in the public healthcare sector ensures no one is left out.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: There are other options, for example, cheaper riders, that they can look at and perhaps, they can convert to those options.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: But in totality, I also want to give the assurance to members of the public and to the Member that no one will be left out or not have access to healthcare, because what is anchoring our healthcare system in Singapore is the fact that there will always be access to subsidised services in the public healthcare sector.

sections.label: Reviewing benchmarks for other cost components
sections.summary: Robust fee benchmarks exist for professional fees, and MOH is reviewing whether to put benchmarks in other components of other costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: On his first point about the components of healthcare costs in the private sector, we are indeed looking at the different dimensions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We already have some robust fee benchmarks on the professional fees front.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We are reviewing to see if there is a need and if there are some ways for us to also put in benchmarks in the other components of the other costs.

sections.label: Insurance cost savings premiums
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked whether it considered policy levers to make insurers pass cost savings to consumers through moderating or reducing premiums, and it says it engages insurers regularly but is mindful about intervening.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Has the Ministry considered policy levers to incentivise insurers to have these cost savings pass on to consumers in the form of moderating premium increases, or even reducing premiums, as opposed to these cost savings directly going to insurers' profit margins?

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We engage the insurance providers quite regularly, but we are very mindful about where we intervene, especially because they need to be competitive and there is a commercial dimension to it, which we feel that we should respect.
